column1: # Every piece in the design's own 2D cutting file, measured: the reference for
# this tool's bill of materials, panel development and internal structure on
# SOURCE: "20260429 gnuC2-23 (2D).dxf" in the design archive "20260429_gnuC2-23.zip"
#   (Laboratori d'envol, gnuC2-23, version 20260429), supplied with this round;
#   its README calls the DXF files "not edited". Drawn by LEparagliding 3.28
#   "Jardins" (2026-04-26), whose source (leparagliding.f, GNU GPL) the archive
#   carries. Laboratori d'envol publishes its designs and the program that
# METHOD: the frames "for cutting table" (ribs 1-4, upper panels 1-5, lower
#   panels 2-5) and the internal-structure frames (2-4 straps, 2-5 V-ribs,
#   3-6 and 3-7 pieces between ribs, 1-7 rod pockets) of the 2D DXF, which
#   draws loose LINE segments at 1:1 in centimetres; they were joined into
#   outlines, the 35 gaps of 16 microns or less where a strip's far end meets
#   its side closed. A piece is a closed outline at its CUT size: the seam
#   allowance (12 mm at the sides, 22 at the front and trailing edge of a
#   panel, 12 on ribs and the pieces inside the wing; its section 6) is part
#   of the outline. Holes are the closed loops inside a piece and are taken out.
#   Every upper panel is two pieces: the design's 3D shaping (section 29) cuts
#   it across at section point 73, 12.6% of chord behind the leading edge on
#   the upper surface; each piece is listed by itself, front and rear, by its
#   cell (in the rib column), from the centre out; each lower panel is one
#   The front piece of cell 30 crosses itself: the tip rib is flat (section
#   30, thickness 0), so the panel's edge along it runs to the leading edge and
#   back on itself to the intake; its area here is the signed area of that
#   Each piece sewn inside the wing (section 12) is listed by itself and
#   identified by where the program lays it out (its source gives the
#   offsets): a V-rib strip by its anchor rib, side and row; a piece between
#   ribs by its inboard rib and chord position; a strap by its row and inboard
#   rib; a rod pocket by its rib, from the grid it is drawn on, upper and lower
#   (a shark nose: each rib carries an upper rod round the nose and a lower
#   one along the intake, section 21's rod type 3; the upper is the longer)
#   — and each confirmed against the piece the program's own construction
#   gives (docs/internal-structure.md). Trailing-edge mini-ribs by the number
#   the program prints beside each, the rib outboard of its cell.
#   One side of the wing: the whole wing is twice this, the centre rib once.
#   Units: the file's own, centimetres; areas cm2.
#   A rib's perimeter is its cutting line's length, its holes apart.
# CHECKS: rib 1 is its section's area (gnuC2, 235.63 cm chord, 6727.56 cm2)
#   plus 12 mm over its 489.54 cm contour, 7315.0 cm2 against 7317.44; every
#   rib is the program's own construction of its cutting line (its 6.11), to
#   0.0002% of its area and 0.01 mm of its length, the flat tip rib included
#   (141.03 cm2: its line runs out to the nose and back on itself, and the
#   strip starts at the intake); its nine holes are its section 4 drawn as
